title: Astronomers may have discovered a black hole born before the first stars
summary: A mysterious object named Phoebe, detected when it briefly magnified a distant star, could be a primordial black hole formed just after the Big Bang. With an estimated mass only three times that of the Moon, it may be a 13-billion-year-old cosmic relic that offers new clues to the mystery of dark matter.

title: Too much of this common nutrient could be accelerating blood vessel aging
summary: Researchers have uncovered a kidney protein that may hold an important key to vascular aging and longevity. The protein helps prevent excess phosphate from accumulating in the blood and gradually turning flexible blood vessels rigid. In animal models, a deficiency accelerated blood vessel aging and significantly shortened lifespan, while reducing dietary phosphate helped lessen the damage.

title: Deep beneath Australia, hidden caves could unlock the secrets of alien worlds
summary: Scientists have solved the mystery of strange trenches scattered across Australia’s vast Nullarbor Plain, revealing an extensive hidden world beneath the surface. These subtle landscape features are created as deeply buried cave systems slowly collapse upward over millions of years. The discovery could help researchers locate unexplored caves containing ancient environmental records and unusual life forms.

title: World’s largest trial of robotic knee replacement reveals surprising results
summary: Robot-assisted knee replacement surgery offers greater surgical precision, but a landmark clinical trial has revealed a surprising limitation. Despite the advanced technology, patients experienced no meaningful improvements in pain, mobility, or recovery compared with conventional surgery after one year.

title: Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong
summary: Loneliness can be surprisingly deadly, with previous research linking it to a roughly 30% increase in the risk of premature death. However, a new study warns that treating loneliness as a medical condition could distract from its deeper social causes. While healthcare professionals can offer support, lasting solutions may require rebuilding communities and fundamentally changing the way people live and work.

title: Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea
summary: More than a mile beneath the surface of the Red Sea, scientists have discovered rare underwater lakes that could reveal secrets about Earth's ancient oceans and the possibility of alien life. Known as brine pools, these extremely salty, oxygen-free environments are surprisingly teeming with microbial life, challenging our understanding of where living organisms can survive.

title: For decades, scientists may have misunderstood how brain cells work
summary: A major new study challenges a long-standing assumption about how the brain works, revealing that most neurons are versatile multitaskers rather than highly specialized workers. By analyzing recordings from 43 regions of the mouse brain, researchers discovered that although some neurons are dedicated to specific functions, most respond to a wide variety of information in remarkably distinct ways.

title: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men
summary: Men and women appear to be similarly capable of multitasking, but men are more than twice as likely to ignore conversation while juggling multiple activities. Researchers believe this unexpected difference may help explain why women are widely perceived as better multitaskers.

title: This 345-million-year-old fossil had scientists fooled for decades
summary: A famous 345-million-year-old fossil has turned out to be something entirely different from what scientists believed for decades. Advanced X-ray imaging revealed hidden gills and thousands of tiny teeth, exposing a primitive aquatic or amphibious creature rather than an early reptile. The discovery suggests that several adaptations associated with life on land actually evolved in animals still dependent on water.

title: This dietary supplement may have an unexpected benefit for the brain
summary: A naturally derived dietary supplement called urolithin A may help the brain get more oxygen and nutrients when it needs them most. In a randomized clinical trial involving 50 middle-aged adults with obesity, researchers found that taking the supplement daily for four weeks increased blood flow to the brain during a challenging memory task, particularly in a region involved in working memory.

title: Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease
summary: A combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin produced results comparable to antibiotics when used alongside standard treatment for severe gum disease, with benefits persisting long after supplementation ended. The surprising discovery could offer an alternative for some patients while reducing reliance on antibiotics.
